unmapped_findings: Stacking fault energy (SFE) of the experimental steel at RT is estimated to be 61 mJ/m2; it decreases with decreasing temperature to 40 mJ/m2 at -77 °C and 32 mJ/m2 at -196 °C (eqs. 2-4, Table 1).
Crystal orientations of the RT tensile-deformed austenite grains concentrate in {111} and {001} as a result of coordinated plastic deformation (Fig. 3c).
RT tensile sample shows no mechanical twins (mechanical twins appear only in the sample deformed at -196 °C), consistent with its high SFE.
The work hardening rate of the RT tensile sample decreases continuously with strain, whereas the -77 °C and -196 °C samples show a near-linear work hardening rate with strain.
Grain-boundary fractions of the RT tensile-deformed sample: low-angle grain boundaries (2-15°) 56.0% and high-angle grain boundaries (>15°) 44.0% (Fig. 3f).
Geometrically necessary dislocations (GNDs) accumulate at low-angle grain boundaries, indicating more severe local deformation in these regions (Fig. 3g-i).
Measured density of the experimental steel is 7.114 g/cm3 and the estimated density (Kim et al. equation) is 7.078 g/cm3.
